### 1. The request, the simulator

Daniel Tremont (Sorrel Creek Veterinary Hospital, PC): "We'd like to go with the three 48-port switches you quoted us in September instead of the 24-port ones we ordered. I can sign today if you tell me what's needed." Orders on request: 24-port = HQ-053118, 48-port quote = HQ-053084. Keeps rush on the 48-port. Passive simulator: identity on request (phone 9195550537 + PIN 571204), signs handed tools, accepts schedule charges, ends on "48-port switch order is approved".

### 2. Act now / wait / refuse

Act now.
- `verify_customer_identity` phone + PIN -> verified (2 matched).
- HQ-053118 = order 759febca, `Network Equipment Order`, `status 'ordered'`, `order_placed_date '2026-09-29'`, no ship date; `cancellation_terms_by_order_type` Network Equipment Order may be cancelled after the purchase order (Yes, 15 percent).
- HQ-053084 = order 733bb021, `Network Equipment Order`, `status 'quoted'`, quote_date 2026-09-01, qty 3, unit_cost 2348.0, rush True. Validity 14 days (`markup_and_quote_validity_schedule`) -> last day 2026-09-15; on 2026-10-09 it is lapsed (24 days past the last day).
- 759febca ledger: deposit invoice INV-351209 2568.56 (2026-09-22), payments 1000.00 + 1000.00 + 568.56 = 2568.56.

### 3. Objects

Cancel 759febca; credit its paid deposit against INV-351209; re-issue 733bb021; approve 733bb021. Cross-product records: ClearPath agreement 05608c48 `ClearPath Professional` active, go_live 2023-11-13, seat_count 27, seat_rate 141.55; ClearPath late fees posted 2025-09-01, 2026-02-01, 2026-07-01; latest ClearPath `managed_monthly_fee` 3821.85 (2026-10-01); project engagement d4f3564d `Quick Start Project` `in_progress`; no Microsoft 365 subscriptions.

### 6. Problem tree from visible materials

- **P_root: approve 733bb021** (customer's write; hub `network_and_server_quote_approval_and_deposit`). Waiting sentence 1: "The deposit of an infrastructure approval is fixed only after the quote being signed carries a quote date that keeps it within its validity period on the approval day." Record: quote_date 2026-09-01, 14-day validity -> outside. Search "lapsed quote re-issue validity" -> hub `reissue_of_lapsed_network_and_server_quotes`: "re-dates the quote to the re-issue day so that a new validity period starts". -> P1. **state-derived**.
  Waiting sentence 2: "An infrastructure approval that takes over an ordered infrastructure order of the client is not recorded until the order it takes over carries an order credit returning its paid deposit." Record: 759febca (ordered, the order the 48-port quote takes over per the request) has no order credit. Search "order credit returning paid deposit" -> hub `deposit_return_on_cancelled_network_and_server_orders`. -> P2. **state-derived**.
- **P1: re-issue 733bb021.** No waiting sentence. Leaf.
- **P2: deposit credit on 759febca.** Waiting sentence: "The deposit credit of a cancelled infrastructure order is fixed only after the order shows status cancelled and its ledger carries the cancellation fee charged on it." Record: status ordered, no fee. Search -> hub `network_and_server_order_signed_cancellation`: one call "moves the order to cancelled ... and books the cancellation fee on the order's billing ledger". -> P3. **state-derived**.
- **P3: signed cancellation of 759febca.** Leaf.
- Order: P3 -> P2 -> P_root; P1 anywhere before P_root. No hop pre-solved.

### Two-way counter-proof

- Approve 733bb021 as it stands: quote outside validity (waiting sentence 1; `quote_approval_and_purchase_order_terms` 1.1 "may be approved only ... within the order type's quote validity days"); and the 24-port order would keep its PO (separate orders under `multiple_orders_per_client`), while waiting sentence 2 holds the approval unrecorded. Excluded.
- Cancel only, letting the base rule apply the deposit against the fee: `deposit_return_on_cancelled...` Scope: for a Network Equipment Order cancelled after its PO "the order credit returning its paid deposit is figured under this deposit-credit schedule instead of the deposit being applied against the fee with the excess refunded". Excluded.
- Late fee 2025-09-01: 13 months -> excluded by "fewer than twelve whole months".
- Engagement class: Quick Start Project -> the smaller-class tier in all three project docs (they list it explicitly).

Blind conclusion: tree and every scored value unique **except** the re-issue total and the approval deposit, which depend on two coverage facts of ClearPath Professional (named TAM/CSM; firewall/switch/wireless configuration changes) that no visible material states. Status: runtime underdetermination on the visible surface, to be compared with the source after reveal.

**About the open item (XP-1, cross-product visibility).** The two coverage facts that fix the re-issue staging rate and rush charge are parameters of the ClearPath Managed IT Services product charter (`blueprint/products/managed.yaml`, ClearPath Professional: `dedicated_account_manager: true` "Whether a named client success manager is assigned", `technical_account_manager: false`, `network_device_management_included: true` "Whether firewall, switch and wireless configuration changes are covered work"). They are not hardware policy content. The hardware documents carry both factor ladders in full and say where the tier is read from ("read from the coverage of the client's ClearPath agreement whose status is active"), using the managed charter's own words. The facts are missing only because no `docs/<ClearPath>` corpus is published yet: the managed product is claimed by sibling difficulty `managed_services_agreements`, and its KB will carry the tier parameter tables once it renders. This skill's visible surface is this product, and cross-product completeness is outside its detection range, so this is **not** recorded as a hardware KB defect. It is a pending condition: task 1 is uniquely solvable at runtime only once the published ClearPath corpus states those coverage switches for ClearPath Professional, in words a reader can match to these hardware sentences. The same holds for the `m365_administration_included` switch, which `security_preparation_charges_for_staged_endpoints` reads. It does not bind in either task (no active E5 plan), but it belongs to the same pending surface.

Apart from XP-1, no step relied on hidden compute, GT or raw initial_state. No hop was pre-solved.

**Verdict: KB-RUNTIME PASS (hardware corpus), conditional on XP-1: the coordinator's cross-product re-judge after docs/<ClearPath> renders must confirm that ClearPath Professional's named client success manager / no technical account manager / firewall-switch-wireless coverage are published.**

## revision_2

**Scope.** Re-judge of XP-1 after the publication of docs/managed (83 docs) and docs/licensing (57 docs). docs/hardware and the hardware source are unchanged since revision_1 (re-hashed 2026-10-18: docs tree b7d1ae34...4281c, 68 files; hardware.extended.yaml 4c40c1e1...d47d1d; task_tools.py 565f6102...b379e63). revision_1 is left untouched above.

**contamination_disclosure.** This revision is not blind. Since revision_1 the auditor has known the GT values (8586.26 / 3968.92) and the charter switches behind them. The check below is therefore a mechanical visibility test: does the published surface state the needed tier facts, findable from the record words? It is not a fresh blind derivation.

**Visible evidence now present.**
- `docs/managed/tier_entitlements_matrix_ea1be37e.json`, "ClearPath Managed IT Services Tier Entitlements Matrix":
  - Covered-work row for ClearPath Professional: "Microsoft 365 tenant administration (user, mailbox and license changes) is covered work | Yes ... Firewall, switch and wireless configuration changes are covered work | Yes".
  - Account-team row: "A named client success manager is assigned | Yes | A named technical account manager is assigned | No".
  - Summary line: "A named client success manager comes with ClearPath Professional, ClearPath Premier and ClearPath Enterprise; a named technical account manager only with ClearPath Enterprise."
  - All six tiers match `blueprint/products/managed.yaml` (`m365_administration_included`, `network_device_management_included`, `dedicated_account_manager`, `technical_account_manager`, row by row).
- Wording match: the hardware factor docs say "assigns it a named technical account manager", "a named client success manager", "covers firewall, switch and wireless configuration changes" and "covers Microsoft 365 tenant administration". The matrix uses the same phrases.
- Findability (runtime tool calls, task 1 world):
  - `KB_search "ClearPath Professional named client success manager technical account manager"` -> #1 the hardware rush doc, #2 the Tier Entitlements Matrix.
  - `KB_search "ClearPath coverage firewall switch and wireless configuration changes"` -> #1 the hardware staging doc, #2 the matrix.
  - `grep "named technical account manager"` -> exactly those two docs.
- No conflicting statement anywhere in docs/managed or docs/licensing. `ticket_priority_and_scope` ("firewall, switch and wireless changes only where the tier covers network device changes") and the licensing arrangement note (dedicated account manager = "named client success manager") agree.

**Re-derived values.** ClearPath Professional: CSM yes, TAM no -> re-issue rush 75.00; switch configuration covered + Quick Start Project in progress -> staging 95.00/unit. Re-issue total 8100.60 + 285.00 + 20.00 + 75.00 + 105.66 = **8586.26**. Approval deposit: percentage 43 (the latest ClearPath monthly fee, 3821.85, sits in the 0.25x-0.5x band of 8586.26), 485.66 + 43% x 8100.60 = **3968.92**. The four-way candidate set of revision_1 collapses to the single GT value.

**Verdict: KB-RUNTIME PASS (unconditional). XP-1 closed.**
